/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 17 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2878 (15)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4590 (52)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2206 (-22)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1628 (6)
Baltic Handysize Index: 864 (-2)
CAPESIZE
The market made a relatively quiet but generally positive start to the week, with sentiment remaining firm across both basins. The BCI 5TC index advanced by $470 on the day to settle at $41,625, supported by stable underlying tone despite limited fresh activity. In the Pacific, sentiment remained firm, although trading was subdued. The C5 index edged up by 0.125 to $14.235, while some spreads suggested some resistance from charterers. Offers were initially reported in the upper $14s, while one major miner was said to have started bidding in the low $13s before improving to the mid $13s. As the day progressed, offers softened towards the $14.50 level, with indications of $14.30 being discussed by the close, although no fixtures had been confirmed at the time of writing. Three major miners were active in the market today, helping to underpin overall sentiment. In the Atlantic, conditions remained steady and broadly well supported, although activity was limited as many participants appeared content to adopt a wait-and-see approach. South Brazil and West Africa to China started the week quietly, with little fresh business reported. However, market talk emerged of a West Africa to China fixture concluded late last week at $37.00, although details remained unconfirmed. The C3 index posted a marginal gain of 0.085 to settle at $35.980.
PANAMAX
A quiet start to the week was reflected in limited reported fixture activity. Market sentiment remained negative across both basins, placing further pressure on rates and resulting in the P5TC declining by $202 to $19,853. Brokers report that the tonnage list in the North Continent and West Mediterranean remains ample, with Charterers adopting a measured approach as they assess prevailing market fundamentals, while Owners re-evaluate their rate expectations. Activity in the Pacific was also reported to be subdued. Market participants noted that while sentiment has softened today, the market does not appear to be in freefall, with underlying fundamentals remaining relatively well supported. However, some brokers highlighted a growing number of prompt vessels in the South Pacific. Mineral demand from both the North Pacific and East Coast Australia is said to remain stable. Overall, a lack of momentum and ample vessel availability continue to weigh on the market, particularly in the Atlantic, although underlying demand in the Pacific is providing some support to fundamentals.
SUPRAMAX
A usual slow start to a new week with very few trades emerging from Friday. The Index routes were mainly positive with the 11TC average lifting $64 to start the week at $20,572. In the Atlantic the North American market remains steady with a decent amount of inter-Caribs grains concluded last week and the area looking balanced, whilst further south the tonnage list appears to have lengthened and the recent small gains from last week could be in jeopardy. The Continent which has held up quite well without much scrap demand is now looking fragile and the Meditteranean continues to weaken without fresh injection of cargoes to replace those already covered. Sentiment in the East is more positive after small improvements from last week lead by NoPac grains with support from the steels backhauls in the North, whilst South East Asia has seen much more activity albeit without witnessing much increase in rates. The Equinox Dawn II (60,456 2015) prompt in Nansha fixed a trip via North Vietnam to the WC South America intention bagged cement at $18,000, the Selena (63,464, 2020) Guangzhou prompt fixed via Indonesia for a trip US Gulf at $14,300 and Akij Pearl (56,060 2005) open Mombasa 22-27 August was reportedly fixed for a trip via Nacala redelivery Pakistan at various rumoured levels between $20,000 and $21,800 to XO.
HANDYSIZE
The Handy market opened the week on another quiet note, with the BHSI closing at 864 while the 7TC average fell by $26 to settle at $15,553. The Continent and Mediterranean market remained under pressure overall, weighed down by insufficient support and a noticeable shortage of cargoes, leaving rates slightly below previous levels. In the South Atlantic, market fundamentals showed little change, with rates generally holding steady around last-done levels. The US Gulf continued to move slowly, with very limited fixing activity and weak sentiment prevailing. In Asia, despite a gradual increase in tonnage, limited fresh demand helped keep current rates broadly steady, with no significant change in cargo volumes to support higher levels.

Atlantic
The China Spirit (35,097 2013) was reported fixed from St Lawrence to Morocco at around $19,500 by Cam Negoce. A large Handysize was also heard placed on subjects from SW Pass to the Continent with wood pellets at around $19,000 by Ultrabulk, although further details were not confirmed.

Asia
The Devbulk Saliha (31,018 2011) open Mombasa was fixed for a trip via Richards Bay to the Continent in the mid-to-low teens, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Crude Steel Production

Chinese crude steel production declined 3.6% on the year to a five-month low of 76.9 Mt in July, bringing Jan-July output 3.1% lower to 577.4 Mt, National Bureau of Statistics data show. Meanwhile, Chinese blast furnace capacity utilisation averaged around 90% in July, 0.7 percentage points lower month-on-month, while average daily molten iron output remained near flat at 2.4 Mt/day, MySteel data show. Around 37.8% of the 247 sampled mills were in profit on average in July, a 17.8 percentage point decrease from the prior month and the lowest share so far this year.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve lost value today despite a firmer physical market, as the index gains $470. The Aug and Sep contracts dipped the most with 38800 and 39350 sold late on. However, the Oct closed marginally positive with a trading range of 40250-40900 and 38750-39300 Nov. Q4 struggled for liquidity with a lot of the volume cleared as delta for Q4 put options, with most of the weight trading at 39000. Q1 traded between 26650-26850 and Cal27 30850-30950.
